dedupe_keys.name: universal scanning gui tool for tv white space tvws spectrum availability and rf planning

description: This paper presents a generalised graphical tool that evaluates the availability and usability of TV white space channels and their noise levels at each location, so that secondary devices can use vacant broadcast channels to connect remote rural areas without interfering with primary television services. The tool exports the available and usable channels and noise levels to an external dataset file, visualises them interactively, and adds an RF planning and optimisation algorithm that evaluates communication metrics between a TVWS base station and user equipment, including a ray-tracing based choice of the best azimuth and elevation for the base station and user antennas. Producer: Muneer Al-ZuBi and Mohamed-Slim Alouini; version 1 was submitted on 21 November 2024 and version 2 on 24 September 2025 (signal processing category). Coverage: any area for which a geolocation white space database is available. Access: the abstract page gives the paper only; whether the tool can be downloaded was not confirmed, so open_source is recorded as false, meaning no verified open-source release. Licence and cost: not stated for the software; the paper is free and it is under the CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: TVWS operation depends on regulator-approved white space databases, and the paper's results are the authors' case studies. Simulation uses: it supports capacity planning and antenna optimisation of rural broadband links that reuse broadcast spectrum. Related records: the Py1546 implementation of ITU-R P.1546 (model-py1546) and RadioPlanner (platform-radioplanner).
